messages.subject: occu -- visits within years within a time period.
parts:
Hey Unmarked users, 

I want to be sure I'm formatting data correctly and interpreting models appropriately... 

I have a dataset collected over 9 years. About 250 locations. 

Those sites were all visited at least once during a 5-year period in the 80s and at least once again over a 3-year period in the 2010s. 

Some locations have ~ 3 repeat visits within year. Some were visited in more than 1 year during an era (80s or 2010s)

My main question is simple -- what proportion of the 250 locations were occupied in each era. 

I don't care about the occupancy in any single year, because different subsets of sites were visited in an individual year. My only covariate of interest right now is Era; did occupancy change between the 80s and 2010s?

I'm somewhat stymied by how to do this in unmarked though. It seems like I have 1 more layer of a hierarchy than what occu can handle? (usually visits within a season -- but I have visits within a season within an era). 

Does anyone have any suggestions? References to literature? Am I just overthinking this?

Thanks!
Sarah

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] occu -- visits within years within a time period.
parts:
Hi Sarah

I see two possible ways how to address your 'Era' question in unmarked.
(1) Use dynamic occupancy models and then estimate the occupancy status of each site with ranef(). You can then add up the number of sites occupied at least once during each era to obtain a finite sample estimator of occupancy. Not sure about the variance though, could presumably get at it using a bootstrap. This approach allows for the fact that there will likely be colonisations and extinctions within each era
(2) Treat both eras as closed periods and fit either a static model (using occu()) to stacked data, treating era as a factor, or else, again use a dynocc model (with colext()) with just two primary periods.

Given the long period in between the eras and the relatively short duration of each era (btw, does 5 +3 add up to 8 or 9 ?), the latter would perhaps be my preferred approach.

Best regards  --- Marc

parts:
Thanks Marc, 

Haha, yes, I am currently working with 8 years of data. I should have used R to add 5 + 3! 

I was leaning towards stacked data with occu, running each Era separately. 

I'm wondering if it would be worthwhile to drop instances where a point count was repeated in more than 1 year during an era. For example, if a point count location was visited twice in 2012 and 3 times in 2013 -- I could drop the 2012 surveys and limit pseudoreplication..(selecting the year with the most repeat visits or something) because won't occu() see that as 2 different point count locations? 
I could see that being an issue considering that the data set is pretty unbalanced -- Instances like this are much more common in the recent era, where many sites were visited in all 3 years, and uncommon in the historical era. 

At this point, I've probably run everything on the dataset, so maybe it would be fun to compare occu and colext output for just the recent era too.

Thanks again -- 
It's great to be able to bounce questions off of this community -- 

Sarah

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: AW: [unmarked] occu -- visits within years within a time period.
parts:
Dear Sarah,

 

If using occu() (i.e. you fit a static model) I would simply assume closure over the 5 and 3 years respectively. No pseudoreplication then. Assuming closure amounts then to interpret the occupancy parameter as “occupancy sometimes during the entire period over which closure is assumed”, which is 5 and 3 years. Especially given the relatively long interval between these two eras, I think this makes very much sense and is even a desirable interpretation of the occupancy parameter.

 

Best regards  ... Marc
